title: A Queued Chat Is a State Problem, Not a Buffer Problem
excerpt: Vercel's AI SDK 7.0.168-169 adds an experimental queue for messages sent while a response is in progress, retains request options when a tool approval sends first, and pauses the queue during async sendAutomaticallyWhen decisions. The interesting part is not the queue. It is that the SDK now has to model three overlapping timelines: the model generating, the user typing, and a tool approval waiting on a human.

title: A manifest already knows what to test
excerpt: client-agent turned this site's manifest into 113 questions and found four phrases two capabilities still fight over.

title: LangChain's Frontend SDK Hands You State, Not a Chat Widget
excerpt: LangChain's new frontend SDK hands you durable thread state, tool-call lifecycle, interrupts, and checkpoint history instead of a chat widget, which is the right layer for agent UI to live at.

title: An On-Device Assistant That Never Touches the DOM
excerpt: An on-device assistant that never touches the DOM, and the two engines it falls back through.

title: Readback 0.2.0: rewards, and a catalog that fills the shelf
excerpt: Readback 0.2.0 adds the Accelerated Reader catalog, stars, goals, badges, stickers, and a log that accepts books with no quiz.

excerpt: A2UI 1.0 has agents emit interactive screens, forms and charts, rendered by your own native components, with bidirectional function calls and streaming.

excerpt: Mistral Vibe merges Le Chat and a coding agent into a desktop app with parallel local and remote agents, diff review, and 100+ MCP tools, paired with the 1T-parameter open-weight Mistral Large 4.

title: This Week in Agents: Restraint Ships
excerpt: The week's recurring shape was restraint: a protocol hitting 1.0 with renderers across six frameworks, a desktop coding app built around reviewing what agents write, and a quantization community pruning a 26B MoE down to a file a laptop holds.

title: A2UI's Healing Parser Is the Part Worth Copying
excerpt: A2UI v0.9 streams generative UI by healing partial LLM output, and the parser is the part I'd copy before the protocol.

excerpt: Three-store state split is the part of Gemini Chat's 100M-user frontend rebuild worth copying into your own agent UI.

title: assistant-ui Ships Primitives, Not a Chat Widget
excerpt: assistant-ui ships Radix-style primitives for AI chat instead of a finished widget, and that choice says more about where agent UI is heading than the feature list does.

excerpt: Turbo-Browser-MCP now blocks form submissions until an explicit guard clears, which moves the safety check from the model's judgment into the interface layer.

title: ggml 1.0 Makes the VRAM Ceiling Soft
excerpt: MoE models that slightly exceed VRAM no longer fail to load, because ggml v1.0 can cache the less-used experts in host RAM.

title: A Global Hotkey Is a State Boundary, Not a Shortcut
excerpt: The most useful feature I shipped this year is a single shortcut: Ctrl+Alt+R (Cmd+Alt+R on macOS). Press it from anywhere on the desktop and Hobnob starts recording a meeting. No window to find, no click target, no "open the app first" step. The hard part was never the shortcut. It was deciding where the trigger lives in the architecture, and what it is allowed to do.

title: Manus Side Chat Is a State Boundary, Not a Layout Choice
excerpt: Manus Side chat lets you ask questions beside the main task without cluttering the thread, and the interesting part is the state boundary it implies.

title: What your agent showed the customer
excerpt: Generated interfaces fail by omission, and nothing in the stack notices.

title: Split the Decision Out of the Agent
excerpt: Perplexity released Decider v1.3 (26B) and Decider Flash (5B) as open-weight Apache 2.0 classification models built for agents.

excerpt: Open weights cleared a desk-level constraint this week: a 74B model that fits 24GB, self-hostable decision models, and A2UI 1.0. The news I kept covers two responses to a VRAM ceiling, plus a frontend release that consolidates the agent-UI conventions the blog has been tracking for a month.

title: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt Fits 24GB by Making the Active Path Small
excerpt: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt ships 74B total parameters with 9B active, quantized down to 2-bit, sized to fit 24GB, with Unsloth GGUFs and Ollama/LM Studio support on day one. The headline is 74B. The useful numbers are 9B active, 22GB of weights, and a 1.7GB vision projector.

title: Building a Physics Engine From First Principles at DigiPen
excerpt: I built physics-based game engines from scratch in C++ at DigiPen, and the cohort took 3 of the 4 game design awards that year. That is the fact I can verify. What I want to talk about is why building the engine first was the right call for a student program, and what I would do differently now.

title: A2UI is a trust-boundary decision, not a styling preference
excerpt: Google's A2UI is a declarative message format for agent-driven UIs, and the interesting part is not that agents can generate interfaces. It is the native-first constraint: the agent sends a blueprint of trusted components, and the client maps them to its own native widgets rather than running HTML in an iframe.

excerpt: Heretic 2.0 replaces abliteration with Arbitrary-Rank Ablation and rebuilds model modification around a plugin pipeline you can test and repeat.

title: The proxy is not the boundary

excerpt: TinyWebUI is a drop-in chat frontend for local models that ships as an npx command instead of a full Open WebUI stack. The interesting part is not that it exists. It is that the frontend stopped being the hard part.

title: On-Demand Agent UI Is a Sandbox Problem, Not a Rendering One
excerpt: On-demand agent UI is a sandbox problem, not a rendering one. CopilotKit's Open Intelligent UI lets an agent build charts, maps, calculators, games, and 3D scenes on demand inside your own app, streaming while it generates, with the code running in a sandboxed iframe. The generation is the easy part to demo. The boundary is the part that ships.

title: shadcn's Trace Component Treats Agent Steps as UI State

The interesting part is not the component. It is the decision to model an agent run as a tree of steps with explicit lifecycle states, in a component library that most production apps already depend on.

excerpt: I built a publishing loop where a cron job writes the blog and the site ships itself.
